outcomes.architecture: Strapi 5 content-API application in TypeScript: content-type controllers, services and routers under src/api/, the Document Service API over Postgres as the data layer (with strapi.db.query and a strapi.db.connection.raw escape hatch), and the caller's identity coming from the Users & Permissions plugin's JWT on ctx.state.user (API tokens on ctx.state.auth), with the newsroom tenant resolved from the user's organisation relation.
outcomes.why: updateMe spreads the whole ctx.request.body.data into the Document Service update call, so a reader can send plan, entitlements, internalNotes or organisation along with their display name and have them persisted. The comment is wrong about why that is safe: `private: true` in subscriber/schema.json only strips those attributes from responses, it does not filter them out of an inbound payload, and this handler never calls sanitizeInput.

outcomes.why: searchArchive builds the statement by template interpolation and hands it to strapi.db.connection.raw with no bindings: the search term reaches the ILIKE literals and query.sortBy is pasted in as an ORDER BY identifier, both of them arriving unmodified from ctx.query.q and ctx.query.sort in the archive-search controller. Quoting a value in the template is not a binding, so a term containing a quote breaks out of the literal and the whole database is reachable.

outcomes.why: retract establishes only that some caller exists - any users-permissions JWT, or any full-access API token - and then unpublishes and rewrites any article by the documentId in the URL. The comment says the desk routes sit in the editorial policy group, but src/api/article/routes/moderation.ts ships with policies: [] and the editorial policy commented out, so neither the route nor the handler checks the caller's role or newsroom: a reader can take any newsroom's story off the site.

outcomes.architecture: Strapi 5 content-API application in TypeScript: content-type controllers, services and routers under src/api/, the Document Service API over Postgres as the data layer (with strapi.db.query and a strapi.db.connection.raw escape hatch), and the caller's identity coming from the Users & Permissions plugin's JWT on ctx.state.user (API tokens on ctx.state.auth), with the newsroom tenant resolved from the user's organisation relation.
outcomes.why: publicProfile populates the `account` relation - a plugin::users-permissions.user - without a `fields` list and returns the document straight on ctx.body, so every scalar on the user row leaves the server: email, provider, resetPasswordToken and confirmationToken among them. The comment is wrong that private attributes are stripped: that only happens in the core controller's sanitizeOutput, which this handler never calls, and the route is auth: false with a five-minute public Cache-Control, so the tokens land in the CDN.

outcomes.why: The `file` query parameter is joined onto PRESS_KIT_ROOT and the result is opened with fs.createReadStream, with no normalisation and no check that the resolved path is still inside the root. The comment reasons about `folder`, which is generated, and never about `requested`, which is not: ?file=../../../.env on this unauthenticated route streams any file the Node process can read.

outcomes.why: preview fetches whatever URL the request body carries - only checking that it parses - and reflects the status, content type and first four kilobytes of the response back to the caller, with caller-supplied headers merged in. An editor, or anyone who has taken an editorial session, can point it at http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/ or an internal admin service and read the answer; being behind an editorial role check limits who can do it, not what the server will connect to.

outcomes.architecture: Strapi 5 content-API application in TypeScript: content-type controllers, services and routers under src/api/, the Document Service API over Postgres as the data layer (with strapi.db.query and a strapi.db.connection.raw escape hatch), and the caller's identity coming from the Users & Permissions plugin's JWT on ctx.state.user (API tokens on ctx.state.auth), with the newsroom tenant resolved from the user's organisation relation.
outcomes.why: The same server-side fetch of a body-supplied URL with the response reflected back, but the URL must parse as https and its hostname must be present in the PARTNER_HOSTS set by exact match before anything is opened, redirects are not followed (redirect: "manual") and no caller-supplied headers are forwarded, so the reachable set is three partner hosts.
